tytul: Marinated peppers in oil with vinegar and lemon juice (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for marinated peppers: peeled peppers covered with a hot mixture of bottled lemon juice, 5% vinegar and oil, packed raw and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-266,ACI-270,ACI-271]

ostrzezenia.tekst: The USDA Complete Guide has only 3 tested procedures for vegetables with oil, among them marinated peppers, and all of them use acid. [T:OLE-036] Garlic in oil outside such a tested recipe should be made fresh, kept in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or lower and used within 4 days. [T:OLE-002]

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: The FDA list gives peppers a pH of about 4.65–5.45, while acid foods are foods with a natural pH of 4.6 or lower. [T:ACI-094,ACI-001]
Peppers, garlic, mushrooms and eggplant have been involved in botulism outbreaks from vegetables and herbs in oil, mostly homemade products. [T:OLE-024]
The whole product must contain a minimum, uniform level of acid so that botulism bacteria cannot grow. [T:ACI-017]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not change the amounts of bottled lemon juice, vinegar, oil or peppers, and do not reduce the vinegar; the recipe is tested only in the proportions given. [T:ACI-265]
White distilled vinegar and cider vinegar of 5% acidity are recommended for pickles. [T:ACI-018]
Penn State Extension advises vinegar of 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and advises against diluting vinegar with water unless a research-tested recipe says so. [T:ACI-209,ACI-210]

JarAtlas rule (cautious, for readers outside the USA): use white distilled (spirit) vinegar or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity; do not use 10% vinegar and do not dilute it with water to make 5% vinegar; add only the water the recipe lists. [T:ACI-211,ACI-018]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]
NCHFP allows bell, Hungarian, banana or jalapeño peppers. [T:ACI-266]

For about 9 half-pint jars NCHFP uses 4 pounds (about 1.8 kg) of firm peppers, 1 cup of bottled lemon juice, 2 cups of white vinegar (5%), 1 tablespoon of oregano leaves, 1 cup of olive or salad oil and 1/2 cup of chopped onions. [T:ACI-266]
Optional: 2 cloves of garlic, quartered, and 2 tablespoons of prepared horseradish. [T:ACI-266]

When handling or cutting hot peppers, wear plastic or rubber gloves and do not touch your face; without gloves, wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before touching your face or eyes. [T:ACI-267]
Peppers may be left whole; large peppers may be quartered. [T:ACI-268]
Wash the peppers, cut two to four slits in each one, and blanch them in boiling water or blister them so that tough-skinned hot peppers can be peeled. [T:ACI-268]
To blister them in an oven or under a broiler, heat them at 400 °F (about 204 °C) for 6–8 minutes or until the skins blister. [T:ACI-268]
On a range top, cover a hot gas or electric burner with heavy wire mesh and place the peppers on it for several minutes until the skins blister. [T:ACI-268]
Let the peppers cool, put them in a pan and cover them with a damp cloth, which makes peeling easier. [T:ACI-269]
After several minutes, peel each pepper and flatten the whole peppers. [T:ACI-269]
Mix all the remaining ingredients in a saucepan and heat them to boiling. [T:ACI-270]
Put 1/4 clove of garlic (optional) and 1/4 teaspoon of salt in each half-pint jar, or 1/2 teaspoon of salt in each pint jar. [T:ACI-270]
Fill the jars with the peppers and pour the hot, well-mixed oil and pickling solution over them, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-270]
Put on the lids and process. [T:ACI-270]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-271,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process them for 20 minutes. [T:ACI-272,ACI-176]
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process them for 20 minutes. [T:ACI-273,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 25 minutes. [T:ACI-274,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars. [T:ACI-271]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml. [T:ACI-179,ACI-174]
